clue.text: Cut back on expensive clothes, primarily, and start to knit a sweater

indicators.note: back tells us the word for cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of these two words
the start to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shopper resolves to stop buying pricey clothes and knit a jumper instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut back' reads as trimming spending, but 'back' turns the word for cut round; 'primarily' and 'start to' pick opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a type of jumper with a high, close-fitting rolled collar.

clue.text: Blue gastropod

definitions.meaning: a light purplish-blue shade named after the flower
a sea snail, a mollusc of the gastropod class

explanation.definitionFit: Periwinkle is a soft lavender-blue colour, and also a small edible sea snail.

clue.text: Record kept of fuel consumed

definitions.meaning: a journal or diary kept of events
a piece of wood burnt on a fire

explanation.definitionFit: A log is a written record such as a ship's journal, and a log is wood burnt as fuel.

clue.text: Reportedly, has taped jolly posy

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard spoken

parts.note: to have something taped is to know it thoroughly
gay in its older sense means merry or jolly

explanation.surface: Someone apparently filmed a cheerful bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has taped' is slang for having something sorted, so KNOWS, which sounds like NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers, the same thing as a posy.

clue.text: Keeping seat vacant, inspirit all competitors with somewhere to sit

indicators.note: keeping means the second word holds the first inside it

parts.note: to inspirit is to cheer or encourage

indicators.note: vacant empties the word, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the field is everyone taking part in a race

explanation.surface: Saving a spare seat, a spectator encourages every runner from a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties seat to its outer letters, and 'Keeping' puts those inside the word for inspirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a padded leather sofa, something you sit on.

clue.text: A motel owner screened moderates

parts.note: taken as written
Norman Bates runs the motel in the film Psycho, so he is a motel owner seen on screen

explanation.surface: A hotelier in a film calms things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened' is not hiding anything: it places the motel owner in a film, Hitchcock's Psycho.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or die down, the same sense as to moderate (verb).

clue.text: Mexican dish, in a manner of speaking, one has to finish

parts.note: a burr is a regional way of speaking with a rolled r
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish, so to speak, must be eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' reads as a throwaway phrase but gives BURR; 'has' and 'finish' just place TO last.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a flour tortilla wrapped around a filling.

clue.text: A proper Goth is revolting — he ought to know his place

definitions.text: he ought to know his place

indicators.note: revolting suggests rising up and overturning, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: A properly behaved Goth rebels and is told to know his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is revolting' rearranges A PROPER GOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A topographer maps and describes the features of places, so knowing a place is his job.

clue.text: Work as a farrier in Oxford, for example

definitions.meaning: fit iron plates to a horse's hooves
a laced leather type of footwear

explanation.definitionFit: To shoe a horse is a farrier's work, and an Oxford is a type of laced shoe.

clue.text: Show record

definitions.meaning: to show or display, as a face ... surprise

explanation.definitionFit: To register is to show (as a meter registers a reading), and a register is a written record.

clue.text: Work left over, too much for musicians

indicators.note: over says the two pieces before it are turned round as a whole

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An orchestra finds the leftover piece too much to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole charade round; the held text had a stray S before 'musicians', which the page does not print.
explanation.definitionFit: Troppo is the Italian musical direction meaning 'too much', as in allegro ma non troppo.

clue.text: Winding streets to a single male driver?

indicators.note: winding means twisting, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a single means one

explanation.surface: Twisting roads lead a lone man to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding' rearranges STREETS TO into TESTOSTER; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the male hormone that drives male characteristics and behaviour.

clue.text: Dreamy court official's last to join congregation

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: a congregation is a gathering of people

explanation.surface: A court official dozes off just as he is due to join a church congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb to woo; 'to join' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering means idly daydreaming, so it describes a dreamy, absent-minded state.

clue.text: Cap in hand is so deranged

definitions.meaning: a hat taken off and held, no longer worn on top

explanation.walkthrough: 'is so' links the two senses; read literally, a cap in your hand has come off your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap held in the hand is literally removed from the head, and the phrase also means mad.

clue.text: Divine queen, essentially mobile, perhaps

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself, essentially
a mobile is one kind of phone

explanation.surface: A goddess is fundamentally portable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows the mobile is an example of the word needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Persephone is the goddess who became queen of the underworld in Greek myth.

clue.text: One newspaper in US city that's smart

indicators.note: in means the city's letters go round the others

parts.note: NY stands for New York
I is the Roman numeral one
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A single newspaper in New York is described as stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the numeral and the paper inside the city; FT, the Financial Times, is a British daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is an informal word for neat, clever or stylish, all senses of smart.

clue.text: This might account for booze being found on allotment

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the booze is placed on (after) the allotment

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allotment or share
ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A gardener's drinking is explained by beer turning up on his allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a rented garden plot, a false lead here for a share; 'being found on' puts the booze after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning that accounts for something, the explanation behind it.

clue.text: Disasters — naturally in light lingerie

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it
slips are pieces of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A lingerie wearer suffers wardrobe disasters in flimsy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective for the lingerie, but it is the verb meaning to come down and settle; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Landslips are landslides, disasters caused by nature rather than people.

clue.text: Attention seeker curtly announcing close of play?

indicators.note: curtly means shortened, losing a letter

parts.note: saying the show is off announces the end of a play

explanation.surface: Someone craving attention briskly declares the performance over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtly' shortens SHOW'S OFF by dropping its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off is someone who boasts to draw attention to themselves.

clue.text: Lexicographer not getting on with man behind Biggles

indicators.note: not getting means the following word is dropped from the name

parts.note: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 English dictionary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary writer falls out with a children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is the flying hero of boys' adventure books by Captain W. E. Johns; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: W. E. Johns was the author who created the fictional pilot Biggles.

clue.text: Like Aristides, won over a little while ago

parts.note: Aristides the Just was an Athenian statesman famed for fairness

indicators.note: over means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fair-minded Greek has recently triumphed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WON into NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Just now means a moment ago, a short time back.

clue.text: A supporter is supposed to talk informally, having formerly popped in

indicators.note: popped in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: should means is supposed to
to rap is to chat or talk freely
erst is an old word for formerly

explanation.surface: Someone meant to chat casually dropped in earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popped in' puts the archaic word for formerly between the other two pieces; 'having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder strap is a band that holds up a garment or bag, so it acts as a support.

clue.text: Draw up plans for unwanted delivery

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawing up reads the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Someone drafts plans for an unwelcome parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw up' looks like drafting the plans, but it turns MAPS upwards; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited junk email, a delivery nobody asked for.

clue.text: Disinfectant fluid no help?

indicators.note: fluid means the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A disinfectant liquid proves useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' rearranges NO HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, is a classic antiseptic and disinfectant.

clue.text: Little woman getting letters from a minor artist

parts.note: Jo March is one of the four sisters in the novel Little Women

indicators.note: letters from means the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small woman receives mail from a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters from' rearranges A MINOR into ANMIRO; 'getting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was the Catalan surrealist painter and sculptor.

clue.text: Reduced state of princess on stage

indicators.note: reduced means cut short at the end

parts.note: Idaho is a US state

explanation.surface: A diminished nation belongs to a theatrical royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, so a princess seen on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is the title heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Princess Ida.

clue.text: Change for member of youth group once provided with ultimate in finery

parts.note: mods were a 1960s British youth culture of scooters and sharp suits
if means provided that

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the last letter

explanation.surface: A former mod changes after acquiring the finest clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify is to alter or change something.

clue.text: Species that is protected while sea is regulated

indicators.note: regulated means put into a new order, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A creature is safeguarded while the oceans are controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulated' rearranges WHILE SEA; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The sei whale is an endangered baleen whale protected from commercial hunting.
